html:
The Guanaca were an Indigenous people of the central Cordillera in Cauca, southwest Colombia, around the pass of Guanacas on the old road from Popayán over the mountains to the Magdalena valley.

Spanish sources from the 1500s name them among the peoples who fought the conquerors of Popayán. Little is known of their language or way of life. Their lands lay next to those of the Nasa (Páez) and the Misak, and later records tend to treat them as part of the Nasa, who held out in these mountains for a long time against Spanish rule.
sum: The Guanaca were an Indigenous people of the central Cordillera in Cauca, southwest Colombia, around the pass of Guanacas on the old road from Popayán over the mountains to the Magdalena valley.
